title: Inline small-prime panel-kernel + Barrett-constant cache for n=64
description:
Eliminate the per-call panel-kernel function-pointer dispatch + Barrett-constant load overhead that dominates `gemm_row_panel_fn` at small `n` (≈ 50 ns per row-panel call). Closes the residual minpoly gap on `GF(251)/n=64` which the d1dd266c packed matvec landing did not amortize.

## Background

`d1dd266c` landed `crate::gfp::simd_ops::gemm_row_panel_fn` (canonical-byte AVX2 row-panel kernel processing four rows per iteration). At n=256 the kernel amortises across 64 panel iterations and the `GF(251)/256` charpoly cell PASSes (0.63x). At n=64 the kernel only runs 16 panel iterations and the per-call overhead (function-pointer indirection + Barrett constant load + SIMD register spill at the AVX2 boundary) dominates.

## Hard ceilings (fflas-ffpack reference)

| Cell | fflas wall | 1.5x ceiling | Pre-task gf2 wall | Pre-task ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GF(251)/n=64 minpoly | 0.135 ms | 0.202 ms | 0.545 ms | 4.04x FAIL |

## Success Criteria

- [hard] The `GF(251)/n=64` minpoly cell meets the 1.5x ceiling (≤ 0.202 ms) on the current Zen 3 host, **OR is covered by a user-approved scope amendment to the broader 97bf0879 epic per the 2026-05-07 amendment below.**
- [hard] Either: (a) the panel-kernel call site is **lifted from the per-row inner loop to the per-`matvec_packed` boundary** so the runtime SIMD function pointer is loaded once per matvec rather than once per row-panel iteration (full elimination of the runtime-dispatch indirection conflicts with the project's `OnceLock`-based portability contract documented in `CLAUDE.md` § "Unsafe isolation"), or (b) a per-prime Barrett-constant cache amortises the constant load across an entire matvec (rather than per row-panel call), or (c) both. The choice is implementation discretion.
- [hard] No regression on `GF(251)/n=256` charpoly or `GF(251)/n=256` minpoly cells (already tracked by sibling tasks; verify both still pass / improve, do not regress).
- [hard] No regression on the GF(2^31-1) and GF(65521) minpoly/charpoly cells.
- [hard] Correctness: scalar-equivalence proptest comparing the inlined / cached path to the reference scalar matvec for boundary lengths {0, 1, 15, 16, 17, 63, 64, 65}.
- [hard] Final evidence updates `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-d1dd266c-minpoly-tuning.md` (or a successor doc) with the new GF(251)/n=64 minpoly Criterion median + before/after comparison.

## Amendment — 2026-05-07 (user-approved)

Per AskUserQuestion 2026-05-07: 70766cb1 delivered a ~30% gap reduction (0.545 ms → 0.383 ms; 4.04x → 2.84x of fflas), but the residual gap is below the granularity that further inline + Barrett-table tuning can close at this `n=64` boundary. The remaining gap is the per-call AVX2 register/lane setup overhead in the small-n row-panel kernel; closing it requires a bespoke register-scheduled small-n AVX2 kernel.

That work is filed as **`52cce970`** (Bespoke small-prime AVX2 kernel for GF(251) charpoly+minpoly residual cells) and tracked under the broader finite-field LA SOTA catch-up planning issue **`615db3b9`**, NOT as a blocker on this issue.

Empirical basis: `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-d1dd266c-minpoly-tuning.md` § 3.1, § 6.1.

Re-escalation threshold: re-evaluate the GF(251)/n=64 minpoly cell when `52cce970` closes.

## Amendment 2 — 2026-05-07 (user-approved, SC#2 architectural clarification)

Per AskUserQuestion 2026-05-07 (R2 review escalation): SC#2 option (a) — "the panel-kernel call site is inlined at the dispatch boundary so the function-pointer indirection is removed" — is amended to "the panel-kernel call site is **lifted from the per-row inner loop to the per-`matvec_packed` boundary** so the runtime SIMD function pointer is loaded once per matvec rather than once per row-panel iteration".

Empirical basis: full elimination of the AVX2 runtime-dispatch indirection conflicts with the project's `OnceLock`-based portability contract documented in `CLAUDE.md` § "Unsafe isolation" (`gf2-core/src/lib.rs` `simd::maybe_simd()` → optional `LogicalFns`). The `OnceLock` cache is the project's intended contract; eliminating the function-pointer call would require a `target_feature("avx2")` compile-gate that the project does not adopt.

The current implementation lifts the `fns` load to the `PackedFpMatrix::Small` construction site (one read per `matvec_packed`, not per row-panel) and uses a global per-prime `SmallPrimeTables::from_mont` / `to_mont` cache built once via a `OnceLock` (`crates/gf2-core/src/gfp/simd_ops.rs:1180-1208`). This satisfies SC#2 option (a) under the amended reading, and option (b) is independently satisfied by the Barrett-constant cache.

## Notes

Allowed to add a small `#[inline]` hint or a fast-path branch in `crates/gf2-core/src/gfp/simd_ops.rs` and/or `crates/gf2-core/src/gfp/mod.rs`. SIMD register-scheduling work that requires unsafe goes into `gf2-kernels-simd` per project unsafe-isolation rules.
